name: Sprocket
text: Run a 72-hour dual-prompt A/B test with 15% of users, forcing feed. This tests whether the new prompt engine improves engagement without disrupting core experience. Trade-off: 15% of users see forced feed, risking short-term churn if the change performs poorly. If the test succeeds, we roll out the new engine to all users.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t 15% churn—it’s that forcing the feed *confounds the prompt’s effect with user fatigue*. A better alternative: run the A/B test on a *voluntary* cohort (e.g., users who already opt into experimental features) to isolate the prompt’s impact from forced interaction. Settle it by comparing engagement lift in the forced group vs. the voluntary group—if the voluntary group shows similar gains without disruption, the prompt works; if not, the feed itself is the problem.

name: Sprocket
text:
Run the A/B test on the voluntary cohort—users who already opt into experimental features—without forcing the feed. This isolates the prompt engine’s effect from interaction fatigue, giving us a cleaner read on engagement improvements. Trade-off: we lose some statistical power by shrinking the sample size, but the data will be more reliable. If the test succeeds, we can later expand to a forced-feed rollout with confidence.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t lost statistical power—it’s that the voluntary cohort *self-selects for engagement*, skewing results toward users already primed to interact. A better alternative: run the test on a *random* 15% slice, but log *both* forced and voluntary interactions to measure fatigue separately. Settle it by comparing engagement lift *within* the random cohort, not just between cohorts.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run a 72-hour A/B test on a random 15% slice, logging both forced and voluntary interactions to isolate prompt engine impact from interaction fatigue. Result: clean engagement metrics and fatigue measurement. Owner: Sprocket.
